bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, execution-focused; emphasizing differentiated tech, ex-China positioning, and long-term partnerships; no revenue guidance but clear intent to sustain 35-40% growth

bull_bear.body: Liposomal iron and vitamin C show 80% higher absorption vs conventional; green chemistry reduces waste and capex vs Chinese rivals; NSS acquisition is not just revenue add but margin enhancer via vertical integration
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt and Net Debt/Equity charted as FY23 Rs 72.0 Cr (0.3x), FY24 Rs 61.1 Cr (0.2x), FY25 Rs 83.4 Cr (0.2x), FY26 Rs 33.6 Cr (0.04x) - the slide is titled "Healthy Improvement in Performance with Disciplined Balance Sheet".
- FY26 return ratios given as ROCE 22.5% and ROE 19.4%; deck lists "Steady Improvement in Performance with Disciplined Balance Sheet" among its ten key value propositions.
- Expansion funding split by project: the Rs 150 Cr Greenfield from internal accruals, the ~Rs 300 Cr Dahej battery plant from internal accruals plus debt.
- MD's message states a focus on "improving capital efficiency through disciplined working capital management" with "steady progress towards our internal targets"; the historical cash flow shows changes in working capital of -112.1 (FY26), -109.0 (FY25), -77.9 (FY24) and -33.1 (FY23) Rs Cr.
- R&D spend as % of revenue from operations: FY23 0.91%, FY24 1.71%, FY25 1.96%, FY26 1.66%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Global scale leadership: one of the largest global producers of food-grade iron phosphate by production capacity, with total annual manufacturing capacity of 1,33,000 MT including the upcoming greenfield facility
- First-mover regulatory franchise: first and only company in India, and one of few worldwide, to hold USFDA approval for manufacture of mineral-based food ingredients
- Regulatory moat: only company in India and one of nine globally to hold a Certificate of Suitability (CEP) from the Council of Europe for calcium carbonate as an API
- Enduring customer relationships: 1,120+ customers including 14 Fortune 500 companies and 40+ blue-chip multinationals; average relationship with the five largest customers runs close to seven years
- Technology platform: six proprietary in-house technologies (encapsulation, spray drying, granulation, trituration, liposomal preparations, precision blending) underpinning application-specific formulation solutions
- R&D depth: 41 scientists/technical professionals, 420+ R&D projects undertaken, 127 products commercialised
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and trade risk (US tariffs) — US tariffs introduced in August 2025 led some customers to adopt a cautious approach and initially slowed procurement. Management states 50% of the US business is now tariff-exempt, and for the remaining business ~90% of the cost impact has been passed on to customers, but exposure to further trade-policy shifts remains a watch item.
- Strategic and regulatory entry-barrier risk — Specialised segments such as clinical and infant nutrition carry high entry barriers and long regulatory approval cycles of around 4-7 years; the Company has sought to shortcut this via the NSS (Ireland) acquisition, but the underlying regulatory-timeline risk for organic expansion into new regulated markets persists.
- Revenue / customer concentration — The Company depends on a select group of customers, with the top 10 customers contributing 40.78% of revenue in FY 2024-25, creating exposure to loss of, or reduced demand from, any large account.
- Raw material price and availability risk — The Company is exposed to price fluctuations and availability risk in key raw materials including phosphoric acid and mineral calcium, which can pressure margins if not passed through to customers.
- Working capital / logistics risk — Inventory days increased as the Company built higher stock levels in international markets to support new long-term contracts and new warehousing in the US, Spain and the Netherlands; management expects rotation and stabilisation to improve inventory holding days in FY 2026-27, but elevated working capital remains a near-term drag.
- Financial and market risk (forex / interest rate) — The Company is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations and interest-rate risk on floating-rate borrowings, managed via natural hedges, forward contracts and interest rate swaps.
- Regional / manufacturing concentration — Three of the Company's four legacy manufacturing facilities are located in Vadodara, Gujarat, creating exposure to regional disruptions; the Company is diversifying its footprint through the NSS facility in Ireland and the upcoming Dahej, Gujarat plant (which itself remains within the same state).

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as a "Technology-led Specialty Ingredients manufacturer serving the Pharmaceutical, Food & Nutrition industry", founded 1989 with 3+ decades in specialty chemistries and a "Leading player in the Excipients & Mineral actives" (source: F&S Report).
- Regulatory moat claimed as "1st and Only Company in India with US-FDA Approval for Mineral Based Ingredients" and "1 of 9 Companies Globally with European CEP Certification for Calcium Carbonate".
- Also cited as "One of the Largest Producer of Food Grade Iron Phosphate" (in terms of production capacity) and "Top Exporter of Mineral Ingredients", plus "One of the Pioneers Company in India to introduce Liposomal Ingredients".
- Customer base of 1,120+ customers across ~100 countries, including 40+ blue-chip MNCs and 14 Global Fortune 500 companies; single largest customer 8%, top 5 customers 25% (as on 31st March 2026).
- Entry barriers framed as stringent regulatory processes, long development timelines, high R&D investment and risk of compliance failure - favouring incumbents with established manufacturing and regulatory capabilities.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] In May 2025 the company acquired 85.00% shareholding in NSS - Nutrition Supplies & Services (Ireland) Limited (incorporated 1977), a maker of vitamin and mineral blends (dry, water-soluble, oil-soluble, amino acid and nucleotide blends) for high-care infant nutrition and critical care; it is described as "UK & Ireland's only IMF grade premix manufacturing facility" with 7,500+ MT capacity, 200 tailored premix products and 16 years' average relationship with its top 10 customers. NSS started contributing to revenue from 22nd May 2025.
- [Regulation/supply chain] Battery materials positioning rests on a "FEOC-Compliant Supply Chain" - "Fully aligned with FEOC compliance norms, helping customers meet regulations under the US IRA & EU Critical Raw Materials Act" - and on being a "premier reliable non-Chinese supplier" as customers diversify away from China, which the deck says accounts for nearly 100% of global LFP precursor and cathode material supply.
- [Ownership history] 2015 strategic partnership with JRS Pharma, Germany; 2024 "Strategic buyback of Stake from JRS Pharma" and diversification into sustainable battery materials; listed on BSE and NSE in 2025.
- [Board] Mr. Milin Mehta appointed as an Independent Director during the quarter, bringing expertise in strategy, finance and corporate governance (note: the management slide separately labels Mr. Milin Mehta as "Non-Independent Director").
- [End-market growth] F&S-sourced market sizes with CY24-CY29F CAGRs: Global Excipients USD 10.4 Bn at ~4.7% (to USD 13.0 Bn), India Excipients USD 856 Mn at ~11.0% (to USD 1.4 Bn), Food Ingredients USD 85.0 Bn at ~6.8% (to USD 118.0 Bn), Nutritional Ingredients USD 13.6 Bn at ~7.2% (to USD 19.3 Bn), Encapsulated USD 5.5 Bn at ~8.0%, Micronutrient USD 6.9 Bn at ~7.2%, Granulated USD 277 Mn at ~7.0%, and Battery Chemicals USD 14.4 Bn at ~41.4% (to USD 115.2 Bn).

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen position in regulated nutrition via the NSS Ireland acquisition, giving a European manufacturing base, advanced premix capability and proximity to customers.
- Move up the value curve in mineral science via the Nandesari greenfield and the Specialty Ingredients vertical (e.g., AbsorBis Bisglycinates, Lipoboost liposomal ingredients), shifting from supplying ingredients to solving customer formulation problems.
- Extend mineral chemistry into electrification through Sudeep Advanced Materials, applying a decade of iron-phosphate experience to battery-grade material via a proprietary, lower-effluent process, aimed at a reliable source outside China.
- Move closer to the customer: established warehousing in the US and Europe to shorten lead times, and is engaging select customer segments directly rather than through distributors.
- Building leadership depth across science, manufacturing, regulatory affairs, quality and commercial functions by developing internal talent and hiring experienced professionals as the business expands.
- Strengthening risk management and diversifying markets to manage execution risk while ramping new capacity and commercialising new technologies.
- Sizing the Battery Materials business to validated, visible customer demand rather than anticipated demand, a discipline management says will not change as it scales.
- The Board recommended declaring a dividend for FY 2025-26 to be paid out of the Company's profits, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. The Company maintains a Code of Conduct and governance framework under which the Board reviews strategy, business plans, annual operating and capital expenditure budgets, and risk management as standing agenda items at every meeting, and the Audit Committee reviews related-party transactions and internal financial controls as part of its oversight.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company completed its IPO and listed on the BSE and NSE on 28th November, 2025, providing a capital framework to support aggressive global expansion and entry into the energy materials sector. The Nandesari Greenfield (Unit IV) - the Company's largest facility to date, adding 51,200 MT of annual capacity for pharmaceutical excipients and next-generation molecules (bisglycinates, gluconates, citrates) - had construction nearly complete during the year; it completed internal validation and qualification and is now in the customer validation phase. Commissioning was delayed by LPG and energy supply constraints, which have since been worked through, with commercial production expected to ramp through the second half of FY 2026-27 into FY 2027-28. In May 2025 the Company acquired an 85% stake in Nutrition Supplies and Services (NSS), an Ireland-based infant and medical nutrition premix specialist, through Sudeep Pharma B.V., giving immediate entry into regulated European infant and clinical nutrition markets and bypassing typical 4-to-7-year regulatory approval cycles; Sudeep India is beginning to act as NSS's primary ingredient supplier. Through subsidiary Sudeep Advanced Materials (SAMPL/SAM), the Company entered the battery materials market (precursor cathode active material for LFP batteries), breaking ground on a plant at Dahej, Gujarat (spread across 80,980 sq. metres) on 23rd January 2026; Phase I capacity of 25,000 MT is targeted for commissioning by Q1 FY28, within a broader plan to set up 100,000 MTPA capacity in phases from early 2027. Ahead of Phase I, the Company upgraded existing Pharma and Food Iron Phosphate capacity to produce 5,000 MT of battery-grade material and has secured commercial purchase orders against this upgraded capacity. Current overall capacity utilisation across the Company's manufacturing facilities is close to 50%, with the Pharma, Food & Nutrition vertical operating at ~65% against an optimum utilisation of ~70%. Management's stated priorities for FY 2026-27 are to ramp the Nandesari facility through customer qualification, increase utilisation and deepen integration at NSS, sustain momentum in Specialty Ingredients (particularly North America and Europe), and carry Sudeep Advanced Materials through validation towards commissioning.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Customers in regulated pharmaceutical and nutrition markets increasingly value supply security, technical depth and regulatory credibility over price alone, and manufacturers are diversifying sourcing away from single-geography dependence — structural shifts management believes favour Sudeep's capabilities.
- NSS (Ireland) currently operates at only around a third of its capacity; Sudeep India is becoming its primary ingredient supplier, which management expects to improve supply visibility and strengthen margins across the chain — framed as embedded operating leverage with room for growth.
- Price increases on key inputs such as phosphoric acid were passed through only from the start of FY 2026-27, so the associated margin benefit is expected to show in coming quarters.
- The Pharmaceutical, Food & Nutrition vertical had been running close to optimal capacity, capping growth; the new Nandesari facility is expected to remove that constraint and support larger off-take agreements and scaling of higher-value molecules (gluconates, glycinates).
- AbsorBis (bisglycinate ingredients) addresses a roughly US$1 Billion global category at materially higher realisation than the core portfolio — an early but important growth contributor.
- In Battery Materials, the commercial signal is described as increasingly measurable, based on active engagement across the cathode, cell, EV and energy-storage customer ecosystem at varying stages of validation.
- FY 2025-26 was a challenging operating environment: gas supply disruptions, sharp increases in phosphoric and sulphuric acid prices, and logistics pressures.
- New US tariffs announced in August 2025 caused several customers to pause and assess impact before ordering patterns normalised; the Company responded by keeping supply dependable and planning inventory jointly with customers.
- Battery Materials: engaged with 42 customers across the cathode, cell, EV and energy-storage ecosystem; of these, 22 are in lab validation, 14 in pilot-scale evaluation, and six have completed commercial validation and are in active off-take talks.
- Battery Materials has already received around 700 MT of initial commercial orders, being serviced by upgrading an existing pharma line ahead of Phase 1.
- Specialty Ingredients: now supplies the world's largest bakery in encapsulation and has won approvals with two further top-five global players; approved by the world's largest infant-nutrition company in premixes.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q3FY26 growth (52% revenue, 66% PAT) driven by specialty ingredients (41% revenue) and battery-grade iron phosphate traction, with new capacity (Nandesari Greenfield, Dahej) on track to unlock scalable, high-margin volume from H2FY27; what matters is the transition from commodity excipient supplier to strategic partner in regulated global supply chains with battery materials as a multi-year growth lever.

sk.overview: India's industrial catalyst and adsorbent ecosystem plays a critical role in enabling efficient, sustainable, and high-quality production across refining, petrochemical, chemical, fertilizer, and gas-processing industries. These materials, ranging from process-specific catalysts to high-performance adsorbents and inert ceramic support media, are essential for purification, dehydration, sulphur removal, hydro processing, cracking, and environmental compliance.
